what: 望 (wàng): what is trending in Chinese media right now, translated. A feed to explore. Nothing here is scored or read by Prism.
source: Each platform's own public hot list, read directly by chinavision-pull.py. Not read this time: Zhihu: HTTPError HTTP Error 403: Forbidden.
notesBy: Accounts, quotes and reception are written by local:qwen, on this Mac from the news pages it read. Reception comes from three places, each named beside it: the article itself, the hourly roundup published on Sina, and the top comments under the most-watched videos on Bilibili. What is visible is what was allowed to stay up. Accounts are in its own words; a quote is kept only when it is found exactly in its source and is short. The full texts stay on this Mac (data/chinavision/raw/) and are not shown. Read by Claude on 11-20: one headline translation corrected (it had left out America), four comment translations corrected (a character’s name, two nicknames, a term), and two reception summaries rewritten from the comments themselves.

items.zh: 黎曼猜想
items.en: The Riemann Hypothesis [a famous unsolved problem in mathematics]
items.note: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims he and the AI model Claude have proven the Riemann Hypothesis and its generalization, generating over 250,000 pages of text and 17 million lines of formalized code. The article notes that while some experts find the approach promising, the proof has not yet undergone the peer review required by the Clay Mathematics Institute to claim the million-dollar prize. It highlights skepticism regarding the reliability of AI-generated formal code and the timing of the announcement shortly after Anthropic's stock listing.

reception.en: The article reports that Fields Medalist Terence Tao is reviewing the proof, while other mathematicians express cautious confidence or skepticism about the AI-generated code's validity and the announcement's timing.

items.zh: AI证明黎曼猜想通过形式化验证
items.en: AI proves the Riemann Hypothesis through formal verification
items.note: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims to have proven the Riemann Hypothesis and its generalization in collaboration with the AI model Claude, submitting over 250,000 pages of text and 17 million lines of formalized code. While the proof has not been publicly released in full, experts like Terence Tao and Alex Kontorovich have offered preliminary observations, noting the use of advanced mathematical frameworks. The article highlights skepticism regarding the verification process, pointing out that Lean code only checks logical consistency and may not perfectly match the original mathematical conjecture. Furthermore, the claim does not yet meet the Clay Mathematics Institute's requirements for prize consideration, which demand peer-reviewed publication and a two-year validation period.
